title: Head Injury & Concussion
summary: Anyone with a head injury needs watching closely for worsening signs. Assume a neck injury too if the mechanism is significant.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for any of these after a head injury
when: Any loss of consciousness, even briefly
Unequal pupils, weakness, numbness, slurred speech or vision problems
Clear fluid or blood from the nose or ears
Taking blood thinners, or a high-speed / high-fall mechanism

steps.title: Check DRABC
steps.text: If unresponsive and not breathing normally, start CPR.

steps.title: Suspect a neck injury
steps.text: If the mechanism could have injured the neck (vehicle crash, fall from height, diving), ask them to keep still.

steps.title: Control bleeding
steps.text: Scalp wounds bleed a lot. Apply firm pressure with a clean dressing – but use gentle pressure around any depressed area of the skull.

steps.title: Monitor closely
steps.text: Record the time of the injury and check their level of response, breathing and behaviour regularly.

steps.title: Concussion
steps.text: Anyone with a suspected concussion should stop activity (sport, driving, competition) and not return the same day. They should be assessed by a healthcare professional and should not be left alone.

warningSigns: Clear fluid from nose or ears
doNot: Do not let them return to activity or drive
Do not give alcohol or sedating medicines
Do not apply firm pressure to a depressed skull fracture

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
